title: Observability: metrics, tracing tags, dashboards & alerts for data residency enforcement
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
Goal
Add first-class observability for Hosted/Dedicated data residency enforcement so SRE/Security/Support can (a) monitor enforcement health, (b) detect and triage spikes in residency violations, and (c) produce evidence that enforcement is operating as intended.

Scope
1) Metrics
- Add Prometheus counters/histograms for:
  - Residency decision outcomes (allow/deny)
  - Violation reasons (region mismatch, cross-region fallback blocked, downstream write blocked, policy evaluation error)
  - Policy evaluator call behavior (cache hit/miss, fail-closed vs fail-open if applicable)
  - Routing behavior when pinned (attempted fallback, override usage)
  - Downstream write blocks (analytics/log persistence/storage) caused by residency enforcement
  - Error response breakdowns for residency errors (HTTP status + error_code)
  - Latency impact of enforcement middleware (gateway admission check time; policy evaluator roundtrip)

2) Tracing
- Add standard tracing attributes (OpenTelemetry span attrs) on request spans for:
  - residency.enabled (bool)
  - residency.pinned_region
  - residency.allowed_regions (stringified, low-cardinality)
  - residency.request_region (effective region resolved from endpoint / routing)
  - residency.decision (allow|deny)
  - residency.reason (enum)
  - residency.policy_source (org|project|workspace|default)
  - residency.exception_id (if temporary exception applied)

3) Dashboards
- Grafana dashboard(s) under Eng Platform > Compliance:
  - Overview: decision rate, violation rate, deny reasons, top orgs by deny count (guardrails around PII), region distribution
  - Enforcement health: policy evaluator error rate/latency, cache metrics, gateway middleware latency, downstream write blocks
  - Routing interactions: cross-region fallback attempted vs blocked; override usage (allow_cross_region_fallback) gated by feature flag
  - Rollout views: violations split by feature flag cohort (canary vs control), and by org tier

4) Alerts + runbook integration
- Alert rules with rollout-safe thresholds (avoid paging during canary unless clearly broken):
  - Sudden spike in residency denials across many orgs (possible misconfig or bad default)
  - Policy evaluator failures leading to elevated fail-closed denies (or elevated fail-open if ever enabled)
  - Elevated middleware latency / p95 increase for admission check
  - Downstream write enforcement failures (audit pipeline blocked, exporter errors)
- Each alert links to: sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/runbook-residency-violation-spike.json

Non-goals
- Not building customer-facing analytics in Console here (handled under console workstream)
- Not adding long-term compliance reporting exports beyond audit log events (handled under audit exporter project)

Implementation notes / constraints
- Cardinality: avoid org_id as a metric label. Use hashed org bucket or only include org_id in logs/traces. For dashboards requiring “top orgs”, rely on logs/audit event queries or a controlled internal-only data source.
- Residency “allowed_regions” should be normalized to a stable small set (e.g., "eu-only", "us-only", "multi") for metrics; keep full list only in audit events.
- Ensure metrics are emitted on both allow and deny paths (so we can compute total checks and allow rate).

Proposed metrics (final names pending observability standards review)
Counters
- redwood_residency_check_total{decision, reason, pinned_region, request_region, org_tier, product_surface}
  - decision: allow|deny
  - reason: ok|region_mismatch|fallback_blocked|policy_error|downstream_write_blocked|exception_applied
  - pinned_region/request_region: from a bounded set (eu-west, us-east, etc.)
  - product_surface: hosted|dedicated
- redwood_residency_policy_eval_total{result, cache, org_tier}
  - result: success|error|timeout
  - cache: hit|miss
- redwood_residency_cross_region_fallback_total{outcome, org_tier}
  - outcome: attempted|blocked|allowed_override
- redwood_residency_downstream_write_block_total{sink, org_tier}
  - sink: audit_log|traces|analytics|object_storage
- redwood_residency_error_response_total{http_status, error_code, org_tier}

Histograms
- redwood_residency_gateway_check_duration_seconds{org_tier, decision}
- redwood_residency_policy_eval_duration_seconds{org_tier, cache}

Gauges
- redwood_residency_policy_cache_age_seconds (if we expose cache freshness from gateway/router)

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Metrics are present in Prometheus and validated in staging + canary.
- [ ] Metrics conform to Observability Standards (label cardinality review by Allison Grant).
- [ ] Tracing tags show up in Honeycomb/Tempo for both allow and deny.
- [ ] Grafana dashboard exists with at least: violation rate, deny reason breakdown, policy evaluator health, and middleware latency.
- [ ] Alert rules merged into observability-pack with rollout-safe thresholds and runbook links.
- [ ] Support/SRE can answer within 5 minutes:
      - “Is enforcement working?”
      - “Are denials due to customer misconfig or platform regressions?”
      - “Is a specific region having abnormal policy evaluator latency/errors?”

References / related work
- Confluence dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/dashboard-data-residency-enforcement.json
- Runbook: sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/runbook-residency-violation-spike.json
- Alert threshold proposals: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/residency-enforcement-alert-thresholds-sheet.json
- Related PRs:
  - sources/github/redwood/pr_18473.json (metrics + tracing attributes scaffolding)
  - sources/github/observability-pack/pr_417.json (dashboard panels + alert rules)

Open questions
- Do we need a dedicated “rollout cohort” label on metrics (feature_flag_cohort=control|canary)? If yes, confirm label is bounded and set at request admission.
- Should “fail-open” ever exist for Hosted residency enforcement? If not, lock reason enums to reflect fail-closed only.
- Confirm which sinks are in-scope for downstream write enforcement metrics for Phase 1 (audit logs and analytics are must-have; traces might be best-effort).

Planned tasks
- Instrument gateway middleware (Amara) for duration + decision metrics; ensure emitted before model execution.
- Instrument policy evaluator client for cache and duration metrics.
- Add tracing attributes in request context propagation path (gateway -> router -> data plane) with consistent naming.
- Build initial Grafana dashboard JSON + wire to folder.
- Add alert rules with canary-safe thresholds and label filters; coordinate with Rafael Mendes on paging policy.

Risk
- Metric label blow-up due to accidental inclusion of workspace_id/project_id/org_id.
- Noisy alerting during beta if customers misconfigure endpoints/SDK region. Mitigation: alerts should page only on platform-health signals; violation-rate alerts should start as Slack-only with a higher threshold + require broad impact.
comments: 2025-01-13 (Sean Gallagher): Creating as P0 for beta readiness. We need to be able to distinguish (1) customer hitting wrong base URL vs (2) platform routing/policy regression. Please coordinate with Allison on metric naming + cardinality early.

2025-01-16 (Sergio Costa): Drafted dashboard layout + metric set. I’m going to avoid org_id labels; for “top orgs” we’ll use logs/audit queries only. Added proposed metric names to description; will align with observability standards before merge.

2025-01-21 (Allison Grant): +1 on no org_id labels. Also avoid embedding full allowed_regions list as a label. Suggest normalization (eu-only/us-only/multi) for metrics and keep raw list only in audit events/traces.

2025-01-24 (Rafael Mendes): For paging: policy evaluator errors + gateway check latency are page-worthy once canary expands. Violation-rate should be Slack-only at first; otherwise we’ll page on customer misconfig. Please add a “broad impact” alert (many orgs) vs “single org” view in dashboard.

2025-01-28 (Sergio Costa): Opened PR in observability-pack for initial dashboard + alerts (PR_417). Alert rules include runbook links and are Slack-only for violation spikes; paging only for policy evaluator failure + enforcement latency regression.

2025-02-02 (Caleb Johnson): Reviewed tracing attrs. Please use consistent prefix residency.* and ensure attributes are on the root request span (not only internal spans) so support can find them quickly in Honeycomb.

2025-02-05 (Sergio Costa): PR_18473 merged for metrics scaffolding in gateway + routing path. Remaining: tighten label values (region enums) and finalize Grafana JSON + alert thresholds after 48h canary baseline.
2025-02-06 (Sean Gallagher): Marking In Review pending (a) confirm thresholds from the SRE sheet doc, (b) confirm alerts are routed correctly (Slack vs PagerDuty) before enabling canary cohort >5%.
